event.title: Trump Administration Appeals to Supreme Court Over California Ballots
event.canonical_title: Trump Administration Appeals to Supreme Court Over California Ballots
event.summary: The Trump administration has filed an emergency application with the Supreme Court, seeking to block the counting of 20,000 mail-in ballots in California. The administration claims these ballots may belong to non-US citizens, a claim that has been rejected by multiple courts and independent analyses. California officials warn that such a move could disenfranchise eligible voters.

event_overview.title: About California Elections
event_overview.subject: California Elections
event_overview.summary: This event concerns an emergency federal lawsuit seeking to require California and Los Angeles County to segregate vote-by-mail ballots from voters whom federal agencies identified as likely noncitizens, and to verify citizenship before tabulation in the November 3, 2026, general election. The United States relied on the federal prohibition on noncitizen voting, while California officials disputed the reliability of the list and argued that the requested late change would disrupt established election procedures.

facts.label: Election date and administration
facts.value: California’s statewide general election was held on November 3, 2026. County elections officials administer voting and mail vote-by-mail ballots to active registered voters; mailed ballots can be counted if postmarked by Election Day and received by November 10.

facts.label: Federal lawsuit
facts.value: The United States sued California on October 15, 2026, after providing state and local officials a list of more than 20,000 people it described as likely noncitizens. It sought to stop tabulation of their vote-by-mail ballots until citizenship could be verified.

facts.label: Legal issue and requested relief
facts.value: The government invoked 18 U.S.C. § 611, which bars noncitizens from voting in federal elections, and argued that federal law preempted California’s procedures. Its requested emergency relief was an order requiring the state and Los Angeles County to set aside identified mail ballots and verify voters’ citizenship before tabulating them.

facts.label: Court path
facts.value: The emergency dispute moved from the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit and then to the Supreme Court as United States v. California, No. 26A624. On November 2, 2026, the Supreme Court denied the government’s application for an injunction pending appeal.

facts.label: Eligibility and California procedures
facts.value: California requires registrants to be U.S. citizens, and its election system includes voter-registration attestations, signature matching for vote-by-mail ballots, and procedures to challenge eligibility or cancel registrations. The Ninth Circuit’s emergency ruling addressed the government’s requested relief in this case rather than resolving every possible federal-state conflict involving election law.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected timeline covers the immediate emergency litigation over handling identified California mail ballots around the November 3, 2026, election, not the full statewide election, all voter-eligibility enforcement, or the case’s later merits proceedings.
